# What is language?

# Recall



* Linguistics is the study of language
  * ≠ learning many languages
  * ≠ studying a language with the goal of learning to communicate in it
  * ≠ being the grammar police
* More precisely\, linguistics…
  * Is a scientific and systematic approach to understanding how language works
  * Is interested in the structure  _and_  use of language
  * And is focused on the rules that exist in language as observed in use by native speakers
* Descriptive vs\. prescriptive grammar

---

# But what is language?!?

![](images/3-What%20is%20language_0.jpg)



* Last week we said we are talking about language as a distinctly human ability\, not any individual language
  * All humans use language
  * Language may be spoken or signed\, written or not
* According to your book\, “human languages are structured systems for making articulated thoughts fully explicit both internally \(mentally\) and externally \(in a form perceptible to other humans\)” \(p\. 3\)
